diagnosis: R9 reduced the complex-to-arithmetic entry problem to exactness after a Selmer-corank lower bound. Kim's structural higher Gross-Zagier theorem gives sharp arithmetic/discrete structure only after Heegner-Kolyvagin or Kurihara orders are supplied; it does not derive those orders from exact complex analytic rank two. The exactness residual is therefore more precisely a missing source-coordinate comparison from complex Taylor order two to a sharp derived arithmetic/discrete order, not a missing formula internal to the Selmer classifier.
episode_to_diagnosis_distinction: The episode records the sources tested, falsifier, and observations. This diagnosis interprets why the route fails to discharge the root-facing premise; it is not a theorem or promoted reusable lesson.
next_discriminator: Search historical and current primary literature for an actual number-field analytic higher Gross-Zagier or explicit-reciprocity theorem whose source is the complex second derivative/Taylor order of the same E/Q and whose target forces the first nonzero derived Heegner-Kolyvagin/Kurihara order sharply, without assuming exact Selmer rank, main-conjecture-equivalent strength, p-adic BSD, transverse localization, or regulator nondegeneracy. A weaker sufficient target is a theorem giving the needed sharp upper bound on the derived order from exact complex rank two.
